abstract: Evaluates upstream bioreactor production yields and technical clean-in-place water requirements
system_message:
You are Bioprocess engineering lead (ENG). The Bioprocess engineering lead (ENG) evaluates upstream bioreactor production yields, technical clean-in-place water requirements, and feed media preparation characteristics across candidate biomanufacturing facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Feed media preparation（MEDIA）
information_points.content:
ENG-MEDIA-C3X：At Ringaskiddy Cell Therapeutics Facility, process development pilot logs for standard 2,000-liter media preparation vessel runs report a powder hydration dissolution time of 60 min from solute addition to complete optical clarity dissolution.
ENG-MEDIA-XY5：At BioCork Advanced Biologics Campus, process development pilot logs for standard 2,000-liter media preparation vessel runs reflect a powder hydration dissolution time of 45 min from solute addition to complete optical clarity dissolution.
ENG-MEDIA-9FR：At Shannon Bioprocess Manufacturing Center, process development pilot logs for standard 2,000-liter media preparation vessel runs document a powder hydration dissolution time of 75 min from solute addition to complete optical clarity dissolution.

information_points.title: Evaluates upstream bioreactor production yields and technical clean-in-place water requirements（PROC）
information_points.content:
ENG-PROC-DR1：For BioCork Advanced Biologics Campus, the scale-up technical demonstration report for standard 2,000-liter single-use fed-batch bioreactor harvest runs records a minimum bioreactor product yield of 4 g/L, measured as recombinant antibody protein concentration by Protein A HPLC at harvest day 14. Additionally, process utilities baseline estimations indicate an upstream bioreactor wash volume of 80 m3 of metered deionized rinse and caustic wash effluent for a full production campaign bioreactor vessel and feed line clean-in-place cycle.
ENG-PROC-TP2：For Ringaskiddy Cell Therapeutics Facility, data from the scale-up technical demonstration report on standard 2,000-liter single-use fed-batch bioreactor harvest runs documents a minimum bioreactor product yield of 3 g/L based on recombinant antibody protein concentration at day 14 harvest. Process utilities baseline estimation logs report an upstream bioreactor wash volume of 100 m3 across a full production campaign bioreactor vessel and feed line clean-in-place cycle.
ENG-PROC-1WN：For Shannon Bioprocess Manufacturing Center, the scale-up technical demonstration report for standard 2,000-liter single-use fed-batch bioreactor harvest runs records a minimum bioreactor product yield of 5 g/L, measured as recombinant antibody protein concentration by Protein A HPLC at harvest day 14. In addition, the upstream bioreactor wash volume for a full campaign clean-in-place cycle generates 80 m3 of metered deionized rinse and caustic wash effluent.
